mainTopic: When a person's vessel (כלי) acquires items for him, and whether this works in רשות הרבים
overview: The גמרא brings two opinions about when a person's כלי acquires for him the things placed inside it. רב and שמואל say it works anywhere except רשות הרבים, while רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש say it works even in רשות הרבים. רב פפא says they do not really disagree. רב and שמואל mean the real public street, and רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש mean a סימטא, a side alley. The alley is called 'public' only because it is not private. The גמרא supports this from another teaching of רבי יוחנן: a כלי acquires only where its owner is allowed to leave it. The גמרא then quotes a ברייתא about measuring vessels in a sale, which lists different rules for different places. The ברייתא says that a measuring vessel belonging to one party acquires even in רשות הרבים. This seems to challenge the ruling that a vessel cannot acquire in the public street, and the answer comes on the next עמוד.

steps.title: A person's vessel acquires for him anywhere except the public domain
steps.stepSummary: רב and שמואל rule that a person's כלי acquires items placed in it, anywhere except רשות הרבים.
steps.simpleTranslation: A person's vessels acquire things for him in any place, except for the public domain.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states a rule: if something is put into your vessel, you acquire it, unless the vessel is in the public street.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person's כלי works like an extension of his own property, so whatever goes into it becomes his. The one limit is רשות הרבים. This statement belongs to רב and שמואל, whose names appear just before this section.

keyTerms.meaning: Vessels or containers
Acquires (makes something legally his)
The public domain, such as a main street

phrases.english: A person's vessels
phrases.notes: This is the statement of רב and שמואל, whose names appear right before this, at the end of the previous עמוד.

phrases.english: acquire for him in any place,

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּלְיוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם קוֹנֶה לוֹ בְּכׇל מָקוֹם
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person's כלי acquires for him everywhere except in רשות הרבים.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש: even in the public domain
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן and רבי שמעון בן לקיש hold that a person's כלי acquires for him even in רשות הרבים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן and רבי שמעון בן לקיש both say: even in the public domain.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second opinion that seems to disagree with step 1: the vessel acquires even in the public street.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now there is an apparent מחלוקת. רב and שמואל exclude רשות הרבים, while רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש include it. The next step will ask whether they really argue.

keyTerms.meaning: Both of them
Even

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ
phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan and Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish
who both say:
Even in the public domain.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents an opposing view to step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person's כלי acquires for him even in רשות הרבים.

steps.title: רב פפא: they don't disagree, main street versus side alley
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that רב and שמואל speak of the real public street, while רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש speak of a סימטא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: They do not disagree. Here it means the public domain; there it means a side alley.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא removes the argument by saying each side is talking about a different kind of place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the real רשות הרבים the vessel does not acquire, as רב and שמואל say. When רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש said 'רשות הרבים,' they meant a סימטא, a side alley, where the vessel does acquire. So both rules are true, each in its own place.

keyTerms.meaning: They do not disagree
Here... there (each statement refers to a different case)
A side alley off the main street

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read רבי יוחנן's words 'רשות הרבים' as the main street. According to רב פפא, he meant a side alley.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: They do not disagree;
here, in the public domain,
there, in an alleyway.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the apparent contradiction between steps 1 and 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each opinion refers to a different kind of place.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the two pairs of אמוראים argue about the same public street.
steps.terutzMaskana: No argument: the main street does not work, and the side alley does.

steps.title: Why call an alley the public domain?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש would call a סימטא 'רשות הרבים.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And why do they call it 'the public domain'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks about רב פפא's answer: if they meant an alley, why did they use the words 'public domain'?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא's answer creates a wording problem. A side alley is not normally called רשות הרבים. The גמרא needs to explain the choice of words.

keyTerms.meaning: Why?
Do they call it

phrases.english: And why do they call it
the public domain?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the wording implied by רב פפא's answer.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why a סימטא would be called רשות הרבים.

steps.title: Because it is not a private domain
steps.stepSummary: The alley is called 'public' only because it is not private property.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because it is not a private domain.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the alley got the name 'public domain' only because nobody privately owns it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'רשות הרבים' were used loosely, meaning 'not רשות היחיד.' It does not mean the alley is a true public street with all its rules.

keyTerms.meaning: A private domain

phrases.english: Because it is not a private domain.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is called 'public' simply because it is not privately owned.

steps.title: Support from רבי יוחנן: where he may leave his vessels
steps.stepSummary: Another statement of רבי יוחנן shows the vessel acquires only where one may leave it, which fits an alley but not the main street.
steps.simpleTranslation: So too it makes sense, because רבי אבהו said in the name of רבי יוחנן: A person's vessels acquire for him in any place where he has permission to put them. Where he has permission, yes; where he has no permission, no. Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support for רב פפא's answer from another teaching of רבי יוחנן himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן says the vessel works only where its owner is allowed to leave it. You may leave a vessel in a side alley, but not in the busy main street. So when רבי יוחנן said 'even in רשות הרבים,' he must have meant the alley, just as רב פפא said.

keyTerms.meaning: So too it makes sense (introduces support)
To put it down / leave it there
Yes... no
Learn from this (the point is proven)

steps.whatToRemember: A person's כלי acquires for him only where he is allowed to place it: in a side alley, yes; in the main public street, no.

phrases.english: So too it is reasonable,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: as Rabbi Abbahu said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
A person's vessels acquire for him

phrases.aramaic: בְּכׇל מָקוֹם שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ רְשׁוּת לְהַנִּיחוֹ.
phrases.english: in any place where he has permission to put them.
He has permission: yes;
he has no permission: no.
phrases.notes: You may leave things in a side alley but not in the busy street, so רבי יוחנן must have meant the alley.

phrases.english: Learn from this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב פפא's split between the street and the alley.
steps.raayaObject: רב פפא's claim that רבי יוחנן meant a סימטא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי אבהו's report that רבי יוחנן limited the rule to places where one may leave the vessel.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the working principle of the סוגיא: the כלי acquires based on whether its owner has the right to place it there.

steps.title: A ברייתא about measuring vessels in a sale
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא: with a measuring vessel that belongs to neither party, the buyer acquires only once it is filled; if it belongs to one of them, he acquires each portion as it goes in.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: There are four rules for sellers. Before the measure is filled, the goods belong to the seller; once it is filled, they belong to the buyer. When is this said? With a measuring vessel that belongs to neither of them. But if the measuring vessel belonged to one of them, each portion is acquired as it goes in.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move by quoting a ברייתא about measuring vessels, which it will use to test the rules about acquiring with a vessel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the measuring vessel belongs to neither party, the goods pass to the buyer only when it is full. If the vessel belongs to one of them, the buyer acquires every bit right away. Since a vessel acquiring for its owner is involved, the גמרא will soon examine whose vessel this is and where it stands.

keyTerms.meaning: A measuring vessel / measure
Seller
Buyer
In what case are these words said? (introduces a limit on the rule)

phrases.english: Come and hear:
There are four rules regarding sellers:
Before the measure is filled, it belongs to the seller;
once the measure is filled, to the buyer.
In what case are these words said?
With a measuring vessel that belongs to neither of them,
but if the measuring vessel was
of one of them,
first by first, he acquired.
phrases.notes: The buyer gets each portion the moment it lands in the vessel, without waiting for it to fill.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new test of the vessel rules, using a ברייתא about sales.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling of רב and שמואל (as explained by רב פפא) that a person's כלי does not acquire for him in the real רשות הרבים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא lets a party's measuring vessel acquire right away. The גמרא will next ask whose vessel this is and in whose domain it stands, to see whether this fits the rules taught above.

steps.title: The ברייתא limits its rule and lists other locations
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. Its rule about the measuring vessel applies in the public domain or in a courtyard owned by neither party. It then gives different rules for a sale in the seller's domain, the buyer's domain, or a guardian's domain.
steps.simpleTranslation: When is this rule said? In the public domain, and in a courtyard that belongs to neither of them. But in the seller's domain, the buyer does not acquire until he lifts the item or takes it out of the seller's domain. In the buyer's domain, once the seller agrees, the buyer acquires. In the domain of the person the goods were deposited with, the buyer does not acquire until that person agrees, or until the buyer rents their place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is still quoting the same ברייתא it began in the last step. Here the ברייתא tells us where its rule applies and what happens in other places.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule that a vessel belonging to one party acquires each portion as it goes in is said about the public domain and a courtyard owned by neither side. Inside someone's own property the rules change. In the seller's domain the buyer must lift the item or take it out. In the buyer's domain, the seller's agreement is enough. In a guardian's domain, the guardian must agree, or the buyer must rent the spot. The words 'in the public domain' are what the גמרא will use for its challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: In what case are these words said? This limits a rule to certain cases.
The seller's property or domain
The buyer's property or domain
Until he lifts it up, which is the act of acquiring called הַגְבָּהָה
Goods that were deposited with him, meaning a guardian holds them
That he rents the spot where the goods sit

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new source. It is the second half of the same ברייתא from the last step. The 'rule' being limited here is the rule that a vessel belonging to one party acquires each portion as it goes in.

phrases.english: In what case are these words said?
In the public domain, and in a courtyard

But in the seller's domain,
he does not acquire until he lifts it
phrases.notes: 'He' is the buyer, and 'it' is the measuring vessel with the goods inside.

phrases.english: or until he takes it out of his domain.
In the buyer's domain,
once the seller has agreed,
the buyer acquires.
In the domain of that person with whom they are deposited,
he does not acquire until he agrees,
or until he rents their place.

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּמֶּה דְּבָרִים אֲמוּרִים בִּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים וּבְחָצֵר שֶׁאֵינָהּ שֶׁל שְׁנֵיהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes quoting the ברייתא begun in step 7. This supplies the words the challenge will rest on.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that a person's vessel does not acquire for him in the real public street
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא applies its vessel rule to רשות הרבים. This will be used to show that a vessel acquires there.

steps.title: The challenge: the ברייתא mentions the public domain
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points to the words of the ברייתא: 'in the public domain and in a courtyard that belongs to neither of them.' So a vessel belonging to one party acquires even in the public domain.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any case, the ברייתא teaches: in the public domain, and in a courtyard that belongs to neither of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now pinpoints the exact words from the ברייתא that create the difficulty. It does not need the rest of the ברייתא, only this phrase.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said that if the vessel belongs to one party, the buyer acquires each portion as it goes in. It said this about the public domain too. That means a person's vessel acquires for him even in רשות הרבים. This seems to clash with the view that a vessel cannot acquire in the real public street. The answer comes on the next עמוד.

keyTerms.meaning: In any case, it teaches. This is used to point to the key words of a source.
The public domain or public street
That belongs to neither of them

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the next move. The גמרא will need to explain the 'public domain' in this ברייתא, possibly as a סימטא, the way רב פפא explained it earlier.

phrases.english: In any case, it teaches:
in the public domain,
and in a courtyard that belongs to neither of them.
phrases.notes: The point left unsaid is this: so a vessel belonging to one of them acquires even in the public street.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the challenge from the ברייתא quoted in steps 7 and 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that a person's vessel does not acquire in the real רשות הרבים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says that a vessel belonging to one party acquires each portion even in רשות הרבים. This contradicts the claim that a vessel cannot acquire in the public street.
